lines.text: I want? Say I would like!
Many learners say: I want a table for two, please.
Better: I would like a table for two, please.
Would like is more polite than want.
The second! I would like a table.

data.wrong: I want a table for two, please.
data.right: I would like a table for two, please.
data.why: Would like is more polite than want.

en.hook: Do you say “I want” to ask?
en.tip: In Arabic «أريد» is normal, but want sounds too direct, so we say would like: “I would like a table for two, please.” not “I want a table for two, please.”
en.caption: Do you sometimes say this? “I want a table for two, please.” 😅 In Arabic «أريد» is normal, but want sounds too direct in English, so we say would like, and the right sentence is “I would like a table for two, please.” Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
